submission.name: Break Bloom
submission.tagline: A small desktop garden that turns screen breaks into a routine you can shape.
submission.inspiration: We wanted to make short breaks feel approachable for people who spend long stretches working at a computer. A small animated companion seemed more inviting than another timer notification, and we were curious whether users could shape a simple routine from reusable activity blocks.
submission.what_it_does: The desktop prototype lets a user set a work interval and shows a small animated character when it is time to pause. A break screen offers a few hand and wrist exercises with a timer and an encouraging message when the interval ends. We sketched a visual workflow builder for arranging break steps, but it is not connected to the timer yet.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used Python, Tkinter, and Pillow to create the timer window, exercise cards, and animated desktop pet. The timer triggers the break screen, which reads from a small list of exercises and messages; the pet reacts to the timer state. Separately, we made a mock canvas for arranging routine blocks, inspired by visual agent builders, but it does not yet generate or run a routine.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: Transparent-looking desktop windows and keeping the pet in place took experimentation. We also hoped to infer activity from computer use, but platform-specific permissions and hardware differences made that too large for the weekend. The routine canvas and timer remain separate pieces.
submission.accomplishments: We got the timer, break prompt, and draggable character working together as a basic desktop flow. We are pleased that the prototype can offer a choice of exercises instead of only displaying a generic alert.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned Tkinter event handling, basic animation, and how to keep user choices in a simple desktop interface. We also learned from trying a visual workflow canvas that blocks only help when they connect to real behavior, and AI coding assistance needed review to keep the implementation small.
submission.whats_next: We would connect the routine canvas to the timer, add more break activities, and make the companion customizable. Later, we could explore cross-platform activity signals and optional hardware reminders, with clear controls over what the app observes.
